rule: General guidance only, written by the build from well-known public pages (government travel advice 'Local laws and customs' sections, official tourism boards, CDC destination pages) on the checked date. Customs vary by place, community and person and change over time, so always verify locally. Not legal advice. A null section means the build was not sure, and the app says so. Rows with recheck: true are the least certain.

countries.dress: Dress modestly at temples.
countries.photos: Ask before photographing people; some museums and churches do not allow photos or flash.
countries.gestures: Pointing at people is impolite.
countries.public: Eating and drinking on the MRT is not allowed; priority seats are kept free.
countries.alcohol: Drinking in public is generally allowed; smoking is banned in many public places.
countries.water_note: Tap water is treated, but most people boil or filter it before drinking.
good_to_know: Rubbish is collected by trucks at set times, and public bins are rare.
Fines apply for eating or drinking on the MRT.

countries.greetings: Greetings are important and take time; "jambo" or "habari" are friendly openers. Older people are greeted first.
countries.shoes: Shoes usually stay on indoors; in some homes hosts prefer them off, so follow their lead.
countries.dress: Dress modestly, especially on Zanzibar and the coast: cover shoulders and knees away from the beach.
countries.photos: Always ask before photographing people, especially Maasai communities; do not photograph government buildings.
countries.gestures: Use your right hand to give and receive.
countries.public: Public displays of affection are frowned on; take time over greetings.
countries.alcohol: Drinking in public is frowned on, especially on Zanzibar; smoking in public places is restricted.
countries.water_note: Drink bottled or boiled water.
good_to_know: Traffic drives on the left.
Single-use plastic bags are banned.
During Ramadan, be discreet with food and drink in daytime on Zanzibar.

countries.greetings: A firm handshake and eye contact are usual; first names are used quickly.
countries.shoes: Shoes usually stay on indoors; in some homes hosts prefer them off, so follow their lead.
countries.dress: Modest clothing is appreciated at places of worship; remove hats inside.
countries.photos: Ask before photographing people; avoid filming in government buildings and airport security areas.
countries.gestures: Gestures rarely cause trouble, but avoid pointing at people.
countries.public: People queue and keep personal space; eating while walking is common.
countries.alcohol: Drinking alcohol in the street is not allowed in most places, and the drinking age is 21; smoking rules vary by state and city.
countries.water_note: Tap water is treated and generally safe to drink.
good_to_know: Sales tax is usually added at the till, so shelf prices are lower than what you pay.
Distances are large: check travel times between cities before planning.
Rules differ from state to state; check local signs.

countries.greetings: A handshake for first meetings; one kiss on the cheek is common, including between men who know each other.
countries.shoes: Shoes usually stay on indoors; in some homes hosts prefer them off, so follow their lead.
countries.dress: Dress modestly in churches.
countries.photos: Ask before photographing people; some museums and churches do not allow photos or flash.
countries.public: A calm, polite manner is usual; people queue in order.
countries.alcohol: Drinking in public is restricted in some places; smoking is banned in enclosed public places.
countries.water_note: Tap water is treated and generally safe in Montevideo and most towns.
good_to_know: Sharing mate tea is part of daily life.
Dinner is often late in the evening.

countries.greetings: A handshake or a nod is usual; older people are greeted first.
countries.shoes: Shoes come off in homes and often in temples.
countries.dress: Cover shoulders and knees at temples and pagodas.
countries.photos: Ask before photographing people; do not photograph military sites.
countries.gestures: Beckon with the palm facing down; do not touch people’s heads.
countries.public: Public displays of affection are frowned on; speak calmly.
countries.alcohol: Drinking in public is generally allowed; smoking is banned in many indoor public places.
countries.water_note: Drink bottled or filtered water.
good_to_know: Crossing the road: walk at a steady pace so traffic can flow around you.
Carry small notes for markets.

countries.greetings: A handshake is usual and may be held longer than you expect; greet before getting to business.
countries.shoes: Shoes usually stay on indoors; in some homes hosts prefer them off, so follow their lead.
countries.dress: Modest clothing is appreciated at places of worship.
countries.photos: Ask before photographing people; follow park rules on wildlife photos.
countries.gestures: Gestures rarely cause trouble, but avoid pointing at people.
countries.public: Keep valuables out of sight; in parks, stay in your vehicle unless signs allow otherwise.
countries.alcohol: Drinking in public places is not allowed; smoking is not allowed in enclosed public places.
countries.water_note: Tap water is treated in the main cities; in rural areas, and during supply problems, drink bottled water.
good_to_know: Traffic drives on the left.
Load-shedding (planned power cuts) can affect lights and shops: check schedules.
Eleven official languages: a greeting in the local one is welcome.
